scenario: An esports academy admits players if they have either elite aiming skill or elite strategy skill. A 5% wildcard also admits players with neither trait. Coaches conclude the selected class shows a negative association between aim and strategy.

data.description: Admission is based on either independent strength plus a wildcard.

question: Among admitted players, compute (a) P(aiming | strategy, selected), and (b) P(aiming | not strategy, selected). Is the negative association real or induced by selection?

ground_truth.explanation: The admission criterion creates collider bias.

naive_answer: Strong strategists seem less likely to have strong aim, so the skills probably substitute.
naive_trap: Selection on either skill makes the selected sample misleading.
